newsitem.title: PERU: PERU'S CERVESUR ACCUSES BACKUS OF UNFAIR PRACTICE.
newsitem.headline: PERU'S CERVESUR ACCUSES BACKUS OF UNFAIR PRACTICE.

text.p: Peru's second-largest brewer, Cervesur, on Tuesday accused its main rival of unfair practice, claiming UCP Backus deliberately kept Cervesur's beer in the sun before sale.

"We have proved ... that Backus stored and kept our products exposed to the weather in the north of the country to ruin it and affect our image among consumers," Cervesur spokesman Agustin Valencia said in an interview with local radio CPN.
Officials of Backus, the country's leading brewer, told Reuters they were studying the case but had no comment.
Cervesur has presented its charges -- involving about 1,000 liters of beer -- to the courts, where an official investigation has been opened, Valencia said.

Valencia did not explain how his company's beer allegedly came to be stored on Backus property. But local television station Uranio 15 said the accusations included charges that Backus bought the brew and later distributed it to retailers.
Based on its strong presence in the south, Cervesur has a 20 percent share of Peruvian beer sales. Recently it has made an aggressive push to eat into Backus's dominance in the north.

At the beginning of the year, the Backus group formed UCP Backus by merging its sister companies Backus y Johnston, Compania Nacional de Cerveza, Sociedad Cervecera de Trujillo and Cerveceria del Norte. The new company's full name is Union de Cervecerias Peruanas Backus y Johnston SA.
